requirements.title: Code directories are read-only
requirements.criterion: Code directories are read-only for the application runtime in the collected Magento deployment; assess effective runtime identity, permissions, ACLs and read-only mounts.

human_evidence.instructions: Verify code is not writable by the actual PHP/web-server process, including ACLs and mount policy. Deploy-owner write bits alone do not establish runtime write access; do not chmod a deployment recursively from this observation.

requirements.title: Directory listing absent on probed Magento paths
requirements.criterion: Successful responses from the configured runtime endpoint on /media/, /static/, /errors/ and /var/ must not expose recognizable directory-index markup. Scope is these paths at scan time; transport or unsupported responses are inconclusive.

human_evidence.instructions: Successful responses from the configured runtime endpoint on /media/, /static/, /errors/ and /var/ must not expose recognizable directory-index markup. Scope is these paths at scan time; transport or unsupported responses are inconclusive.

requirements.original_criterion: Directory listing disabled; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

requirements.title: Declared backend route differs from admin
requirements.criterion: The collected app/etc/env.php backend.frontName declaration is a valid non-empty route and differs case-insensitively from admin. This assesses the configured backend route; route entropy and actual public reachability require separate evidence.

human_evidence.instructions: The collected app/etc/env.php backend.frontName declaration is a valid non-empty route and differs case-insensitively from admin. This assesses the configured backend route; route entropy and actual public reachability require separate evidence.

criterion_history.criterion: Non-default admin path (not /admin); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

requirements.title: Admin 2FA core and provider modules declared enabled
requirements.criterion: In app/etc/config.php, the Magento_TwoFactorAuth module and at least one configured Magento admin 2FA provider module are declared enabled; this predicate assesses declared module state only.

requirements.title: Configured admin session lifetime is at most 900 seconds
requirements.criterion: The effective default-scope Magento admin/security/session_lifetime setting resolved from env.php, config.php, core_config_data or actual installed module defaults is a positive integer not exceeding 900 seconds.

requirements.title: Admin URL exposure restricted
requirements.criterion: Admin URL exposure restricted; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Verify the effective admin route and active reverse-proxy/firewall allowlist; repository ACL hints do not prove access restriction.

requirements.title: Configured admin login CAPTCHA or bounded lockout
requirements.criterion: Default-scope Magento admin login configuration enables native CAPTCHA for backend_login, recognized backend_login reCAPTCHA, or a positive lockout failure limit at most 10 with a positive lockout threshold. Locked env.php/config.php settings precede core_config_data. Custom authentication enforcement and runtime effectiveness require separate evidence.

human_evidence.instructions: Default-scope Magento admin login configuration enables native CAPTCHA for backend_login, recognized backend_login reCAPTCHA, or a positive lockout failure limit at most 10 with a positive lockout threshold. Locked env.php/config.php settings precede core_config_data. Custom authentication enforcement and runtime effectiveness require separate evidence.

criterion_history.criterion: Login rate-limiting / CAPTCHA enabled; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

requirements.title: No direct PHP superglobal references in inspected application files
requirements.criterion: Valid PHP files in the configured app subtree contain no T_VARIABLE references to $_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST, $_COOKIE, $_FILES or $_SERVER. Comments and literal strings are ignored. This is a source coding policy, not proof of input validation.

requirements.title: Forms include CSRF tokens (form_key)
requirements.criterion: Forms include CSRF tokens (form_key); assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Verify server-side CSRF validation and exemptions for each state-changing route; token markup alone does not prove CSRF protection.

requirements.title: SSRF protections present
requirements.criterion: SSRF protections present; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Trace attacker-controlled URLs to outbound requests and verify scheme, destination and redirect validation; nearby keywords do not prove SSRF prevention.

requirements.title: No eval/assert/dynamic execution
requirements.criterion: No eval/assert/dynamic execution; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Review dynamic execution arguments and runtime PHP semantics; boolean assert and nearby request tokens do not prove code injection.

requirements.title: Path traversal protections
requirements.criterion: Path traversal protections; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Trace untrusted file paths and verify canonicalization and containment at the actual filesystem sink.

requirements.title: Secure file upload handling
requirements.criterion: Secure file upload handling; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Review effective upload validation, storage and execution restrictions including delegated framework validators.

requirements.title: Use CSPRNG; avoid weak PRNG
requirements.criterion: Use CSPRNG; avoid weak PRNG; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Determine which generated values are security-sensitive and verify their entropy source; ordinary rand usage is not a cryptographic vulnerability.

requirements.title: No unsafe raw crypto or session APIs in custom code
requirements.criterion: No unsafe raw crypto or session APIs in custom code; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

human_evidence.instructions: Review cryptographic algorithms, parameters and session configuration; raw OpenSSL or sodium use is not automatically unsafe.

requirements.title: Force HTTPS in admin and storefront
requirements.criterion: The observed HTTP storefront root and declared backend.frontName entrypoint redirect directly with 301/302/303/307/308 to same-host HTTPS. This is an entrypoint probe, not a universal guarantee for every deployment route.

human_evidence.instructions: The observed HTTP storefront root and declared backend.frontName entrypoint redirect directly with 301/302/303/307/308 to same-host HTTPS. This is an entrypoint probe, not a universal guarantee for every deployment route.

requirements.title: Observed HTTPS response has HSTS max-age of at least one year
requirements.criterion: A successful same-host HTTPS response at the configured runtime URL emits one unambiguous Strict-Transport-Security header with an exact integer max-age directive of at least 31536000 seconds. Repository web-server declarations are not runtime proof.

requirements.title: Runtime endpoint rejects legacy TLS
requirements.criterion: The assessed runtime host and port must accept TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and reject TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Rejection requires peer protocol-version alerts or successful active protocol enumeration; client-side protocol restrictions and connection failures are not proof.

human_evidence.instructions: The assessed runtime host and port must accept TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and reject TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Rejection requires peer protocol-version alerts or successful active protocol enumeration; client-side protocol restrictions and connection failures are not proof.

requirements.original_criterion: TLS protocols >= 1.2; assess only the collected Magento deployment scope.

requirements.title: Literal HTTP asset references absent in assessed markup/CSS

In REMOTE mode, successful HTTPS pages at configured paths must contain no literal HTTP subresource/form references. Dynamic code-generated URLs, external stylesheets and unvisited routes require separate assessment.

human_evidence.instructions: In LOCAL mode, readable markup/CSS files under app must contain no literal HTTP subresource or form-action references. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, and to require the response's Content-Type header field value to match the destination resource. requirements.title: All application components (including load balancers, firewalls, and application servers) determine boundaries of…
requirements.criterion: Verify that all application components (including load balancers, firewalls, and application servers) determine boundaries of incoming HTTP messages using the appropriate mechanism for the HTTP version to prevent HTTP request smuggling. In HTTP/1.x, if a Transfer-Encoding header field is present, the Content-Length header must be ignored per RFC 2616. When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, if a Content-Length header field is present, the receiver must ensure that it is consistent with the length of the DATA frames.

requirements.title: PCI A3.3.1.1: Failures of any critical security control systems are responded to promptly
requirements.criterion: For the applicable assessment scope, verify this complete obligation: Failures of any critical security control systems are responded to promptly. Processes for responding to failures in security control systems include: ; Restoring security functions. ; Identifying and documenting the duration (date and time from start to end) of the security failure. ; Identifying and documenting the cause(s) of failure, including root cause, and documenting remediation required to address the root cause. ; Identifying and addressing any security issues that arose during the failure. ; Determining whether further actions are required as a result of the security failure. ; Implementing controls to prevent the cause of failure from reoccurring. ; Resuming monitoring of security controls.

requirements.criterion: For the applicable assessment scope, verify this complete obligation: Reviews are performed at least once every three months to verify BAU activities are being followed. Reviews are performed by personnel assigned to the PCI DSS compliance program (as identified in A3.1.3), and include: ; Confirmation that all BAU activities, including A3.2.2, A3.2.6, and A3.3.1, are being performed. ; Confirmation that personnel are following security policies and operational procedures (for example, daily log reviews, ruleset reviews for network security controls, configuration standards for new systems). ; Documenting how the reviews were completed, including how all BAU activities were verified as being in place. ; Collection of documented evidence as required for the annual PCI DSS assessment. ; Review and sign-off of results by personnel assigned responsibility for the PCI DSS compliance program, as identified in A3.1.3. ; Retention of records and documentation for at least 12 months, covering all BAU activities.

requirements.title: Configured admin password minimum is at least eight
requirements.criterion: The collected admin password minimum declaration, or the installed Magento User validator minimum when no declaration overrides it, is at least eight characters. This checks the observed admin policy, not every user password or ASVS conformance.

requirements.title: Declared project debug settings are disabled
requirements.criterion: Inspected default-scope project Magento debug/inline-translation declarations and project PHP ini display_errors/display_startup_errors and Xdebug declarations must not enable debug output. Absent declarations are not enabled declarations in this scope; web-worker runtime, custom integrations and all-component ASVS conformance are outside this predicate.

requirements.title: No configured secret patterns in deployed application files
requirements.criterion: Eligible deployed working-tree text files within configured paths and exclusions contain no configured secret-pattern matches. Git history is outside this basic deployment check. Runtime credential configuration app/etc/env.php is excluded; unreadable or oversized eligible files are collection errors.
